answer.rationale: Competitive pressure and doubled churn conversations in price-sensitive SMB segment create urgency that justifies near-term tactical response. Memory 73 confirms targeted promotional pricing drives acquisition and revenue lift in SMB; memory 31 shows simplification also works but addresses different friction (friction at signup vs. price sensitivity). A small guarded test of promotional pricing on the most at-risk cohort can stem immediate churn while preserving the ability to layer other proven tactics (activation messaging from memory 91, onboarding shortcuts from memory 86) once the price floor stabilizes. Enterprise sales assist and referral programs do not address the immediate competitive threat in SMB. The primary risk is that promotional pricing may set expectations that erode unit economics or margin structure; a small test allows measurement of true elasticity before broad rollout. Uncertainty is preserved by not committing to broad rollout or long-term pricing changes until we observe actual retention and qualified revenue impact under genuine competitive pressure.
